name: Victorian (1890)
note: 90 cm Mangin or Schuckert projectors on the continental battleships, not less than six on a large ship (1894), plain carbon arcs (a crater of 1.6-1.8e4 cd/cm2), a 3 deg beam, trained at the light, to search for torpedo boats [SRC]; the boats a small one [EST].

name: Pre-dreadnought (1904)
note: Russia's six 75 cm Mangin lights in pairs (the fore bridge, amidships, the after bridge or the mainmast) with electric remote control, 40 cm on the boats, 1898-1905 [SRC]; the other navies' of the period by it [EST].

name: RN pre-dreadnought (1904)
note: 24-inch on the big ships (landed from the tops to the shelter deck in 1906), 20-inch on the destroyers, each trained at the light [SRC]; the count [EST].

name: Great War (1914)
note: 36-inch plain arcs on the big ships (searchlight towers by the funnels, the bridge's wings; the RN's from mid-1915), 24-inch on the destroyers, each light trained by its own crew to orders by voice pipe ('never really efficient', the RN at Jutland) [SRC]; the count [EST].

name: RN post-Jutland (1918)
note: As in 1916, now four 36-inch over a searchlight control position with directing sights (August 1917) [SRC].

name: German Great War (1914)
note: Plain arcs kept (the navy rejected Beck's high-intensity arc: worse in the Baltic mist), iris shutters, the lights trained dark from a control position before they were switched on: the lights that found the 4th Flotilla at Jutland, 'much more powerful than ours' (Jellicoe) [SRC]; the 110 cm and the count [EST].

name: USN high-intensity (1918)
note: 36-inch high-intensity arcs (Beck in Texas 1914, the 1917 specification's 5e4 cd/cm2 and more, Sperry's 9e4), eight on a battleship, distant electric control, tied into fire control by 1918; the beam's spread about 2/3 the plain arc's [SRC/INFERRED].

name: Interwar (1930)
note: High-intensity arcs everywhere, fewer and bigger lights, trained from control positions [EST].

name: Second War (1940)
note: 150 cm (44-inch in the RN) high-intensity lights slaved to the fire-control directors [EST].

name: RN Victorian (1890)
note: 24-inch projectors with plain carbon arcs on the bridges, the fighting tops and the flying deck, to search for torpedo boats [SRC]; the count and the boats' [EST].

name: RN dreadnought (1910)
note: Twin 24-inch mountings (St Vincent, Colossus, Iron Duke), not 36-inch, hand-worked to orders by voice pipe, until the 36-inch lights of mid-1915 [SRC]; the count [EST].
